title: Feeds, Filter Bubbles and Responsible AI Use
subject: digital

sections.body: Social media feeds are ranked by ALGORITHMS that predict what keeps you engaged: likes, watch time, shares. Outrage and extremes often get more engagement.
A FILTER BUBBLE forms when you mostly see views you already agree with. It can make other views seem rare or extreme.
Break the bubble: follow reliable sources from different perspectives, check the 'why am I seeing this?' options, and search directly instead of only scrolling.
Using AI responsibly: follow your school's or employer's rules, cite AI help, check facts (AI can invent sources), and never paste private data into AI tools.

quiz.q: Why might your feed show increasingly extreme content?
options: Algorithms reward engagement, and extreme content often gets more
hints: What does a feed's algorithm want you to do?
If a TV channel learned that shocking clips kept you watching longer, what would it show more of?
quiz.explain: Algorithms rank content for engagement, and extreme or outrage-provoking content often gets more.

quiz.q: Which is responsible AI use for a school report?
options: Citing that you used AI and checking its facts
hints: AI can be wrong or invent references.
If a friend helped proofread your essay, you'd acknowledge it if required. AI is the same.
quiz.explain: Be open about AI help, and check everything it says.

quiz.q: Which action does the most to break out of a filter bubble?
options: Following reliable sources from a range of perspectives
Liking more posts that match your views
Scrolling your feed for longer each day
hints: A filter bubble forms when you mostly see views you already agree with.
What would make your feed show more variety, rather than more of the same?
Worked example: if a music app only plays one genre because you only ever 'like' that genre, deliberately choosing playlists from other genres widens what it suggests.
quiz.explain: Choosing reliable sources from different perspectives (and searching directly) widens what you see. Liking more of what you already agree with, or scrolling longer, teaches the algorithm to show you more of the same.
